result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.set_node_attrs_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Set attributes on all selected nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L7042-L7116){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.set_node_attrs_ws(**attributes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Updates or adds attributes to nodes in the current selection. Existing attributes are preserved unless explicitly overwritten. Requires an active node selection. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [**attributes]{.doc-parameter-name} : Attribute name-value pairs to set on selected nodes. Each keyword becomes an attribute name, and its value becomes the attribute value. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Attributes are applied only to nodes currently in the selection, and existing attributes not mentioned in the call are left untouched: ::: {#781d3712 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_node('A', value=10) graph.add_node('B', value=20) id_a = graph.get_id_from_label('A') id_b = graph.get_id_from_label('B') (graph .select_nodes_by_id([id_a, id_b]) .set_node_attrs_ws(color='red', importance=0.9) ) graph.get_node(id_a).attributes['color'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 'red' ``` ::: ::: The original `value` attribute survives untouched, since this call never mentioned it: ::: {#d3bde106 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node(id_a).attributes['value'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 10 ``` ::: ::: Combining this with `select_nodes()` makes it easy to tag nodes matching a condition first, then apply attributes only to the matches: ::: {#6da0a77f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A", value=10) .add_node(label="B", value=20) ) ( graph .select_nodes(lambda n: n.attributes.get('value', 0) > 15) .set_node_attrs_ws(category='high') ) graph.get_node_attrs("category") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {2: 'high'} ``` ::: :::
